Additional field evidence from #2546 arm 2 p5_fits, same file, same problem space: the poller's log-staleness arm is STRUCTURALLY BLIND during a fan-out phase, so the CPU-advancing override is the only thing keeping the verdict right.

Observed 2026-08-27 during a healthy p5_fits fan-out:

  poller watches      /workspace/logs/issue-2546.log
  workers write to    /workspace/issue2546/work/fits_a2/slot0..3.log
  result              last_log_mtime_sec_ago = 2134 while all four workers were computing
  verdict             correct, but ONLY via the #518/#658 CPU-advancing override

So during fan-out the poller has no real progress signal at all; it infers liveness from session
CPU. That is exactly the inference this task is asking you to put a rate floor on, which makes the
two halves interact: if the override gains a floor but the staleness arm stays blind, a fan-out
phase whose workers ALL wedge would present as stale-log plus low-CPU and be indistinguishable
from the phase simply being between log writes.

Suggested addition to the same fix, at your discretion: let the poller take a progress signal from
the per-worker slot logs (newest mtime across a phase's worker log glob) rather than only the
dispatcher log. That converts the fan-out case from CPU-inference back into direct evidence.

## The rate separation, now measured in the OTHER direction too

This task's original evidence was the wedge side (~0.9 CPU-sec/min). Here is the healthy side of
the same phase, measured on a cumulative basis over a ~1800 s window:

  session_cpu_secs   9,040 -> 58,455   =  ~1,650 CPU-sec/min  =  ~27 cores sustained

Against the deadlock's ~0.9 CPU-sec/min that is a ~1,800x separation, wider than the ~65x I
originally reported from the single-core refit. A rate floor has an enormous margin to work with;
the sign test has none.

Also confirmed here: GPUs idle is NOT evidence of trouble on this phase. The poller posted its
gpu-idle advisory (all 4 GPUs idle 30 min during healthy phase=p5_fits) while the phase was
verifiably healthy at ~27 cores, because P5's fits allocate no CUDA context at all (0 percent AND
0 MiB across 8 samples over 56 s). The separate plan-side defect that causes it is filed as #2624;
noting it here only so a future implementer does not treat GPU idleness as a wedge term.

Do NOT touch the live #2546 arm-2 pod.

CORRECTION from the filer, and it matters for the probe design: the CLOSE-WAIT-with-unread-bytes signal FALSE-POSITIVES on a healthy compute phase. Even the two-term conjunction I requested does. The CPU RATE FLOOR is the only term carrying the discrimination.

## What I claimed

In #2546 marker v176 I wrote: the one signal decisive alone is a CLOSE-WAIT socket holding UNREAD
bytes with nothing draining it. This task's body asks for that probe as its own verdict, in
conjunction with near-zero interface rx.

## The falsifying observation, same pod, same phase, healthy

Probing a worker I suspected of stalling in #2546 p5_fits (it had not logged a new unit in ~1.17 h):

    worker 54991    cpu_ticks_delta = 36,181 over 30 s  =  12.06 CORES saturated
                    state = R (running), wchan = 0, threads = 129
                    cumulative CPU highest of the four workers

Unambiguously healthy and computing hard. Simultaneously, on the same pod:

    19 sockets in CLOSE-WAIT
    THREE of them holding Recv-Q = 25 unread bytes, owner pid 54485, no reader
    interface rx = 4,968 bytes / 30 s  =  ~166 bytes/s   (near-zero)

So BOTH terms of the requested conjunction were satisfied while the phase was at full compute. The
sockets are leftovers from the finished HTTP staging prelude: the staging code is done with them, so
nothing drains them, and they sit in CLOSE-WAIT holding a TLS close-notify or trailer indefinitely.

## What survives, and what must change

  DOES NOT SURVIVE   the socket signature as a standalone verdict, and the
                     socket + near-zero-rx two-term conjunction as filed in this task's body
  SURVIVES           the CPU RATE FLOOR, which is this task's primary request and which classifies
                     the case above correctly and trivially: 12 cores is not 0.9 CPU-sec/min

Concretely: any wedge verdict MUST include the per-process CPU rate term, and the socket probe can
only ever be corroborating evidence layered on top of a rate-floor trigger — never a trigger itself.
A phase that has finished network work and moved to compute is the NORMAL steady state of this
pipeline, and it satisfies both socket terms permanently.

Note the per-process detail too: the healthy CPU was on the WORKER pid (54991) while the stale
sockets belong to the PARENT (54485). A probe that reads sockets from the parent and CPU from
nowhere, or CPU from the parent only, can miss that the work has moved to children. Read the rate on
the process doing the work.

## Running tally of my own wedge signals that turned out worthless alone

    futex-thread count       wedge ~18/18    healthy download 91/92        useless alone
    CLOSE-WAIT present       wedge yes       healthy refit yes             useless alone
    low CPU delta            wedge flat      healthy download 3 ticks      useless alone
    CLOSE-WAIT + UNREAD      wedge yes       healthy compute yes (THIS)    useless alone
    socket + near-zero rx    wedge yes       healthy compute yes (THIS)    useless as a pair

Four of the five signals I originally offered are now falsified as standalone or paired triggers. The
rate floor is what is left, which is a reason to implement this task narrowly rather than broadly.
